title: Scalar compatibility and linearity of completed coefficient automorphism pullback
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $d=(A,I)$ a Noetherian adic coefficient datum with finite perfect quotients as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use its chosen small pro-etale site, $A_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$, and the coefficient map $s_X:\underline A_X\to A_X$ whose $n$-th projection is the constant quotient map. Let $e:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ be an automorphism. Write $\rho_A:\underline A_X\to e_*\underline A_X$ for the map sending every constant section to itself, and $c_A:e^{-1}\underline A_X\to\underline A_X$ for its adjoint [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $c_e:e^{-1}A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ be induced by the canonical inverse-image limit comparison [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] and the analogous structure isomorphisms $c_{P_n}:e^{-1}(P_n)_X\to(P_n)_X$ for $P_n=A/I^n$; thus $c_e$ is the isomorphism $c_u$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] for $u=e$ and the system $(A/I^n)_n$. Write $c_e^\#:A_X\to e_*A_X$ for the adjunct of $c_e$.

The coefficient scalar squares commute:
$$c_A;s_X=e^{-1}(s_X);c_e,\qquad s_X;c_e^\#=\rho_A;e_*(s_X).$$
In particular, if $s_U(b)$ denotes the scalar section induced by $b\in A$ on a pro-etale object $U$, the sectionwise adjoint equation is $(c_e^\#)_U(s_U(b))=s_{u_e(U)}(b)$, where $u_e$ is base change along $e$. Give module Hom groups the $A$-action through these sections [def-weil-linear-category]. The module direct image with ring action via $c_e^\#$, its specified left adjoint $e^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and their exact induced derived functors are additive and $A$-linear. For any finite tuple generating $I$, the full subcategory of intrinsically complete objects [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is preserved by the ordinary K-flat derived pullback $Le^*$ along $c_e$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and its restriction $H_{\mathrm{comp}}$ is additive and $A$-linear: $H_{\mathrm{comp}}(bf)=bH_{\mathrm{comp}}(f)$ and $H_{\mathrm{comp}}(f+g)=H_{\mathrm{comp}}(f)+H_{\mathrm{comp}}(g)$.

proof.text:
Put $P_n=A/I^n$, write $r_n:\underline A_X\to(P_n)_X$ for the constant quotient map, and $\pi_n:A_X\to(P_n)_X$ for the actual limit projections. By definition $s_X;\pi_n=r_n$. By the profinite-coefficient inverse-image theorem (system $Q_n=P_n$, finite by the datum), $c_e;\pi_n=e^{-1}(\pi_n);c_{P_n}$, where $(P_n)_X$ is the constant ring sheaf of $P_n$ (that theorem identifies it with the sheafified $\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$ of the datum) and $c_{P_n}$ is adjoint to the map fixing constant sections, i.e. the structure map of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Under this identification $r_n$ is the constant-sheaf map of the quotient $A\to P_n$, so clause 3 of the isomorphism inverse-image theorem gives $c_A;r_n=e^{-1}(r_n);c_{P_n}$. Consequently
$$c_A;s_X;\pi_n=c_A;r_n=e^{-1}(r_n);c_{P_n}=e^{-1}(s_X);e^{-1}(\pi_n);c_{P_n}=e^{-1}(s_X);c_e;\pi_n.$$
The projections of the sectionwise compatible-family limit are jointly injective, proving $c_A;s_X=e^{-1}(s_X);c_e$. All these are the actual coefficient maps in the statement.

proof.text:
Let $\eta$ be the sheaf inverse-image adjunction unit. By the adjunct formulas $c_e^\#=\eta_{A_X};e_*(c_e)$ and $\rho_A=\eta_{\underline A_X};e_*(c_A)$. Unit naturality and Step 1 give
$$s_X;c_e^\#=\eta_{\underline A_X};e_*(e^{-1}(s_X);c_e)=\eta_{\underline A_X};e_*(c_A;s_X)=\rho_A;e_*(s_X).$$
Evaluate this equality on a constant section $b\in A$ over $U$. The defining formula for $\rho_A$ sends it to the constant section $b$ over $u_e(U)$, so $(c_e^\#)_U(s_U(b))=s_{u_e(U)}(b)$. This also fixes which scalar action is being used on direct image.

source.place: Second sentence: adjunct scalar equation; Stacks 0H7J, constant sections, and the unit/counit definition of structure maps

proof.text:
Write $G$ for module direct image. Its underlying section map on a module morphism $f:M\to N$ is $(Gf)_U=f_{u_e(U)}$. The $A_X(U)$-action on $GM(U)$ is through $(c_e^\#)_U$. Step 2 therefore identifies multiplication by $b$ on $GM(U)$ with multiplication by $s_{u_e(U)}(b)$ on $M(u_e(U))$. Hence for $x\in M(u_e(U))$,
$$(G(bf))_U(x)=s_{u_e(U)}(b)f_{u_e(U)}(x)=(bGf)_U(x).$$
Similarly $(G(f+g))_U(x)=f_{u_e(U)}(x)+g_{u_e(U)}(x)$ and $G(0)=0$. These identities commute with restriction because the sections $s_U(b)$ do. Thus $G$ is additive and $A$-linear for the stipulated Hom actions.

source.place: Second sentence: scalar compatibility of the actual module direct image; Stacks 03D7 and its specified ring action

proof.text:
Put $F=e^*$, the specified left adjoint of $G$, and let $\zeta_M:M\to GFM$ be its unit. For $h:FM\to N$ its adjoint is $\alpha(h)=\zeta_M;G(h)$. Step 3 and bilinearity of composition make $\alpha$ additive and $A$-linear; it is injective by the adjunction. For $u:M\to M'$ unit naturality gives $\alpha(Fu)=u;\zeta_{M'}$. Since $\zeta_{M'}$ is an $A_X$-module morphism, for parallel $u,v$ and $b\in A$,
$$\alpha(F(bu))=(bu);\zeta_{M'}=b(u;\zeta_{M'})=\alpha(bFu),$$
$$\alpha(F(u+v))=(u+v);\zeta_{M'}=\alpha(Fu+Fv).$$
Injectivity yields $F(bu)=bFu$ and $F(u+v)=Fu+Fv$; the same calculation with zero gives $F(0)=0$. This proves linearity for the specified left adjoint without choosing a different presentation of it.

source.place: Second sentence: module-adjunction linearity; Stacks 03D7, natural Hom bijection

proof.text: The underlying sheaf inverse image of $e$ is an equivalence by the isomorphism inverse-image theorem. The completed coefficient structure map $c_e$ is invertible by the profinite-coefficient inverse-image theorem: it is the inverse-image limit comparison followed by the limit of the constant quotient isomorphisms. Thus this is an equivalence of ringed topoi on the chosen small sites. Apply ringed-presentation transport with both rings equal to $A_X$ and structural map exactly $c_e$. Its module adjunction is the same $F\dashv G$ as in Step 4, and is an exact equivalence. In particular $F$ and $G$ preserve finite limits and finite colimits, as required for the exact-functor derived-linearity theorem.

source.place: Second sentence: exact coefficient transport; Stacks 03CR equivalence case and 03D7, via the existing ringed-presentation transport theorem

proof.text: Give $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ the induced $A$-linear structure from the linear-abelian-derived-category theorem. Apply the exact-linear-derived-functor theorem to each of $F,G$: the coefficient ring $A$ is commutative, the module categories are abelian, the small-site universes are those fixed in the datum, exactness is Step 5, and additivity and $A$-linearity are Steps 3 and 4. It follows that their termwise induced unbounded derived functors are additive and $A$-linear on all derived morphisms, not only on chain maps.

proof.text: Fix any finite tuple generating $I$. Apply the automorphism-completion-unit comparison to this datum, $e$, and the coefficient map already used above. Its hypotheses are precisely the Noetherian datum, additive-torsion $A/I$, finite perfect quotients, and the chosen small site in the statement. It gives preservation of the full subcategory where the intrinsic completion unit is invertible, for this generating tuple and every representative. The functor of that theorem is the ordinary K-flat derived pullback $Le^*$ along $c_e$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], not the termwise functor of Step 6. It is $A$-linear by ringed derived-pullback linearity, with $R=A$ and $s_A=s_B$ the global scalar sections $b\mapsto s_X(b)$: its hypothesis that $c_e$ carries $e^{-1}s_X(b)$ to $s_X(b)$ is the adjunct form of Step 2 on the final object, since $c_e^\#=\eta_{A_X};e_*(c_e)$ and $\eta$ sends a global section to its inverse image. Restrict $Le^*$ to the preserved full subcategory. Its Hom sets, scalar actions and addition are inherited unchanged. Thus for parallel maps of complete objects, $H_{\mathrm{comp}}(bf)=bH_{\mathrm{comp}}(f)$ and $H_{\mathrm{comp}}(f+g)=H_{\mathrm{comp}}(f)+H_{\mathrm{comp}}(g)$, as asserted.
